blocks.text: Surface tension is a property of liquids that describes the force acting along the surface of a liquid, causing it to behave like an elastic sheet. This force arises due to the intermolecular forces between the molecules at the surface.

Molecules at the surface experience a net force inward due to intermolecular forces, leading to a "skin" on the surface. Liquids tend to minimize their surface area due to surface tension, which explains why droplets form spheres. Surface tension influences various phenomena, such as, capillary action, wetting of surfaces and formation of droplets and bubbles.
